subject.title: [Feature]: First-class multi-instance management for Docker installs

question: Should OpenClaw core own first-class Docker instance create/list/delete/update commands, or should multi-instance Docker remain manual Compose/profile operation plus external helper wrappers for now?
rationale: The request adds official operator UX and lifecycle state across Docker, Compose, ports, persistence, updates, deletion, and isolation boundaries; current source shows no narrow implementation gap that ClawSweeper can safely finish automatically.

options.title: Sponsor minimal core lifecycle
options.body: Approve a small explicit core design for named Docker instances with identity, ports, persistence, update/delete, docs, and sandbox-isolation contracts before implementation.

options.title: Keep manual primitives
options.body: Keep the current profile/env/Compose and ClawDock helper story while leaving this open as design backlog for future setup ergonomics.

options.title: Route to wrapper first
options.body: Decline core ownership unless a missing core API is proven, and ask contributors to maintain a wrapper around the current primitives.

recommendation.title: Sponsor minimal core lifecycle
recommendation.body: Approve a small explicit core design for named Docker instances with identity, ports, persistence, update/delete, docs, and sandbox-isolation contracts before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The history points most strongly to steipete for multi-gateway guidance and the setup/security product boundary this decision would define.
